Let me create a comprehensive analysis report. ## Routing Analysis Report: Next.js Dictionary Default Landing Page Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's a complete understanding of how routing works in this Next.js application: ### 1. Current App Router Structure **Root Level:** - `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/app/page.tsx` - Main entry point showing cluster selection UI (links to `/{clusterId}`) - `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/app/layout.tsx` - Root layout with global providers **Dashboard Layout:** - `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` - Dashboard wrapper with Sidebar and Header components - Uses a **route group** `(dashboard)` which doesn't affect the URL structure **Dynamic Cluster Route:** - `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/app/(dashboard)/[clusterId]/` - Dynamic segment for cluster selection - Contains a `page.tsx` file that serves as the **current default page** **Nested Routes:** ``` /[clusterId]/ ├── page.tsx (Current default - shows Dashboard with cards) ├── dictionary/page.tsx (Dictionary management) ├── cluster/page.tsx (Cluster info) ├── indices/page.tsx ├── collections/page.tsx ├── management/ │ ├── jdbc/page.tsx │ ├── pipeline/page.tsx │ └── scheduler/page.tsx ├── search/ │ ├── query-test/page.tsx │ └── reference-ui/page.tsx └── users/ ├── page.tsx └── roles/page.tsx ``` ### 2. Current Default Page Behavior **File:** `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/app/(dashboard)/[clusterId]/page.tsx` **Current Content:** ```tsx "use client"; import { RunningIndexCard } from "@/components/dashboard/running-index-card"; import { WarningIndexCard } from "@/components/dashboard/warning-index-card"; import { IndexResultsTable } from "@/components/dashboard/index-results-table"; export default function DashboardPage() { return (

); } ``` **Current Behavior:** When a user accesses `/[clusterId]` (e.g., `/dev-cluster`), they see a Dashboard page with index cards and a results table. ### 3. Dictionary Page Structure **File:** `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/app/(dashboard)/[clusterId]/dictionary/page.tsx` **Content Summary:** - Full dictionary management interface with sidebar navigation - 9 menu items: OVERVIEW, STOP (stopwords), USER, ENGLISH, UNIT, SYNONYM, UNIT_SYNONYM, SPACE, COMPOUND - Uses `useState` for menu item selection - Dynamically renders content based on active menu using `DictionaryOverview` and `DictionaryList` components - Interactive sidebar with icons and badge indicators - Full client-side component (`"use client"`) ### 4. Navigation and Routing Patterns **Sidebar Navigation:** - File: `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/components/layout/sidebar.tsx` - Currently only has ONE menu item: "Dictionary" linking to `/{clusterId}/dictionary` - Uses `useParams()` and `usePathname()` from `next/navigation` for client-side routing - Highlights active page based on pathname matching **User Flow:** 1. Root page (`/`) shows cluster selection 2. Click cluster → navigates to `/{clusterId}` → shows Dashboard (default) 3. Click "Dictionary" in sidebar → navigates to `/{clusterId}/dictionary` → shows Dictionary ### 5. How Redirects/Default Routes Are Handled **Current Implementation:** - **No explicit middleware or server-side redirects** - This is handled through Next.js App Router's file-based routing - The `page.tsx` file in `/[clusterId]/` is the default page served when accessing that route - Sidebar provides the only navigation mechanism (currently only Dictionary link) **Key Observation:** - There is **no `redirect()` function** used (from `next/navigation`) - There is **no middleware.ts** file that could handle route redirection - The routing is purely **file-based** - Next.js serves the nearest `page.tsx` file ### 6. Changes Needed to Make Dictionary the Default Page **Option 1: Simple File Swap (Easiest)** 1. **Rename/Replace** the current `/[clusterId]/page.tsx` to contain the dictionary page content 2. **Move** dictionary-specific code from `/[clusterId]/dictionary/page.tsx` to `/[clusterId]/page.tsx` 3. **Remove** or redirect `/[clusterId]/dictionary` route 4. Update sidebar links if needed **Option 2: Server-Side Redirect (Cleaner Architecture)** 1. Keep current structure as-is 2. Create `/[clusterId]/page.tsx` with a `redirect()` call: ```tsx import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'; export default function ClusterDefaultPage({ params }: { params: { clusterId: string } }) { redirect(`/${params.clusterId}/dictionary`); } ``` This would automatically redirect users accessing `/[clusterId]` to `/[clusterId]/dictionary` **Option 3: Keep Both, Change Default Behavior** 1. Update `/[clusterId]/page.tsx` to render Dictionary component 2. Keep `/[clusterId]/dictionary/page.tsx` as an alias 3. Update navigation in sidebar to point to root instead of `/dictionary` ### 7. File Paths Summary | Path | Type | Current Purpose | |------|------|-----------------| | `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/app/page.tsx` | Root entry | Cluster selection | | `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` | Layout wrapper | Dashboard frame (Sidebar + Header) | | `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/app/(dashboard)/[clusterId]/page.tsx` | **Current default** | Dashboard with cards | | `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/app/(dashboard)/[clusterId]/dictionary/page.tsx` | Sub-route | Dictionary management | | `/Users/admin/project/admin/search-admin-ui/src/components/layout/sidebar.tsx` | Navigation | Menu items and routing | ### 8. Important Architecture Notes - **Route Groups:** `(dashboard)` is a route group that doesn't affect URL structure but organizes layout scope - **Dynamic Routes:** `[clusterId]` is a dynamic segment capturing the cluster ID from the URL - **Client Components:** Both dashboard and dictionary pages use `"use client"` since they have interactivity - **No Middleware:** This is a simple client-side routing setup without server-side route interception - **Navigation:** Uses Next.js Link component and `usePathname()` for active state detection This setup makes it very straightforward to change which page is the default - simply by modifying the content of the `/[clusterId]/page.tsx` file or redirecting it to the dictionary route.
